curatorBrief.title: Welcome to Letter Sound Group 2!
curatorBrief.intent: Welcome kindergarten learners to Group 2 letter sounds (c, k, e, h, r, m, d). Explain that letters are pictures for sounds in our spoken words. Note that 'c' and 'k' share the /k/ sound. Set the stage for meeting the new sounds while keeping our Group 1 favorites (s, a, t, i, p, n) strong and active.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Letter-Sound Group 2: c, k, e, h, r, m, d. Introduce the new sounds (/k/, /ĕ/, /h/, /r/, /m/, /d/) while systematically reviewing the sounds from Group 1 (s, a, t, i, p, n). Practice problems must pull from the full 13-letter cumulative list.

components.title: Meet the New Letter Sounds
components.intent: Introduce the new letters and their primary sounds with friendly, vibrant visual anchors: 'c' and 'k' making /k/ (cat and kite), 'e' making /ĕ/ (egg), 'h' making /h/ (hat), 'r' making /r/ (sun/ring), 'm' making /m/ (moon), and 'd' making /d/ (dog).

components.title: Letter Spotter: Group 2 Search
components.intent: Direct Instruction letter recognition game where the live tutor prompts the child to spot, find, and match lowercase and uppercase letters across Group 2 and cumulative Group 1 letters (s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d).

components.title: Sound and Blend Explorer
components.intent: Allow students to tap phoneme tiles from Group 2 along with Group 1 review letters to blend simple, accessible CVC words like 'cat', 'red', 'hen', 'men', 'kit', and 'map', hearing individual phonemes and the blended word.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Independently produce the most common sound for each letter in this cumulative set, when shown its grapheme. Assess without first saying its sound: s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d.

components.title: Say the Sound & Link the Letter
components.intent: Direct instruction interactive practice with live tutor audio. The student is shown graphemes from the cumulative set (Group 1: s, a, t, i, p, n; Group 2: c, k, e, h, r, m, d) and independently produces or matches the correct letter sound.

components.title: Sound Out Loud Practice
components.intent: Spoken direct instruction drill where the child sees a printed letter from the cumulative list and speaks the sound aloud into the microphone. Focus especially on holding and producing continuous sounds such as /m/, /r/, and short vowels /ĕ/, /ă/, /ĭ/ alongside review sounds /s/, /n/.

components.title: Caregiver Sound Hunt at Home
components.intent: Guide caregivers in conducting a fun, screen-free letter-sound scavenger hunt using household objects starting with the 13 cumulative sounds (e.g., cup, keys, egg, hat, rug, mug, dish, sock, apple).

finalAssessment.title: Cumulative Letter Sound Showcase
finalAssessment.intent: Assess recognition, letter-sound correspondence, and initial sound matching across the complete 13-letter cumulative pool (s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d) with warm spoken-first prompts and picture choices.

cards.title: Cat and Kite
cards.definition: Letters C and K make the same clicking /k/ sound!
cards.timelineContext: New letters after S, A, T, I, P, N.
cards.originStory: Two different letters teamed up to share one clicking sound.
cards.curiosityNote: Your throat makes a quick click when you say cat!
cards.visualPrompt: A cheerful orange kitten sitting in soft green grass, batting playfully at a bright red diamond kite, storybook illustration, bold outlines, warm morning sunlight.

cards.title: Egg and Hat
cards.definition: Letter E says /eh/ and letter H breaths out /huh/!
cards.timelineContext: Building words with our new letter friends.
cards.originStory: Little chick hatched with an /eh/ sound wearing a hat.
cards.curiosityNote: Hold your hand out to feel warm hat breath!
cards.visualPrompt: A cute fluffy yellow chick popping out of a speckled eggshell while balancing a tall purple party hat on its head, playful cartoon style with pastel colors.

cards.title: Dog on Moon

cards.definition: Letters R, M, and D make roaring, humming, and drumming sounds!

cards.curiosityNote: Press your lips tight to hum like a happy dog!

data.title: Sound Safari!
data.description: Get ready to look at some letters and say their sounds out loud!
data.gradeLevel: kindergarten students (ages 5-6) - Use clear language, relatable examples, foundational skills, and engaging visuals. Encourage exploration and basic problem-solving.

data.title: Sound Safari: The Letter Hunt Adventure
data.subject: Language Arts
data.topic: Phonics: Letter-Sound Group 2 (c, k, e, h, r, m, d)
data.overview: Step into the boots of a sound explorer to track down household treasures starting with the letter sounds /c/, /k/, /e/, /h/, /r/, /m/, and /d/! Caregivers and young learners will build sound clue cards and search their living space to connect letters to real-world objects. This playful hunt reinforces phonemic awareness and initial sound recognition through movement and multisensory play.
learningObjectives: Identify and pronounce the target letter sounds: /c/, /k/, /e/, /h/, /r/, /m/, and /d/.
Match household objects to their correct initial letter sounds with scaffolded guidance.
Distinguish between target letter sounds and previously learned group 1 sounds (s, a, t, i, p, n).

materials.item: Kid-safe household items starting with target sounds

steps.title: Create Your Sound Badges
steps.instruction: Work with your helper to write one lowercase letter clearly on each paper card: c, k, e, h, r, m, and d. You can also add review letters like s and a.
steps.tip: Writing in lowercase is best because young readers see lowercase letters most often in storybooks.

steps.title: Warm Up Your Safari Voice
steps.instruction: Hold up each sound badge and make the letter sound together. Tap your lips for /m/, feel the puff of air for /h/, and feel your tongue bounce behind your teeth for /d/.

checkpoint.question: Can you say each letter sound clearly without adding an 'uh' sound at the end (say /m/ instead of 'muh')?

steps.scienceNote: Isolating pure sounds (clip the vowel at the end) helps children blend sounds smoothly when reading full words later.

steps.title: Set Out on the Sound Safari
steps.instruction: Carry your basket and pick two sound cards to search for first (like 'h' and 'c'). Walk around the room to discover safe objects that begin with those sounds.
steps.tip: Start in the kitchen or bedroom where items like hats, cups, rugs, or spoons are easy to spot.

steps.title: Sound-Check Your Findings
steps.instruction: When you pick up an item, say its name slowly: 'c-c-cup.' Check if the first sound matches your card, then place it inside your collection basket.

checkpoint.question: How many items have you safely gathered in your sound basket so far?

steps.title: Crack the Tricky Sound Twins
steps.instruction: Look at the letters 'c' and 'k'. Notice that both make the /k/ sound! Place your cup next to 'c' and your key next to 'k'.
steps.scienceNote: In English, 'c' and 'k' share the same sound (/k/). Explaining this early prevents confusion during early spelling activities.

steps.title: Mystery Sound Match-Up
steps.instruction: Empty your basket onto a rug or table. Lay out all the letter cards and match each item directly on top of its letter card.

checkpoint.question: What clues in the word help you decide which letter card belongs to each object?

steps.tip: If a word feels tricky like 'egg', emphasize the first short vowel sound /e/ together.

reflectionPrompts.question: Which letter sound was the easiest to find around your home, and what object did you discover?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Identify and pronounce the target letter sounds
reflectionPrompts.hint: Think about everyday things you wear or use in the kitchen.

reflectionPrompts.question: What does your mouth, lips, or tongue do differently when you make the /m/ sound compared to the /d/ sound?
reflectionPrompts.hint: Try pressing your lips tight together for one, and tapping the roof of your mouth for the other.

reflectionPrompts.question: If you had to find an item for a friend that starts with /h/, where in the house would you look first?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Match household objects to their correct initial letter sounds
reflectionPrompts.hint: Think about where you keep things that go on your head or keep you warm.

documentationPrompt.instruction: Line up all your letter cards in a row with their matching household objects underneath. Take a top-down photograph of your complete safari collection.
documentationPrompt.suggestedCaption: I went on a Sound Safari and matched [number] objects! My favorite match was the letter [letter] for [item name].

extensions.title: Silly Safari Sentence Challenge
extensions.description: Pick three items from your basket (like a hat, a mug, and a dish) and make up a funny sentence using all three words.

extensions.title: Mystery Sound Bag
extensions.description: Have your helper hide one item inside a pillowcase. Reach in, feel the shape without looking, name the object, and shout out its beginning letter sound before pulling it out.

safetyNotes: Adult helper recommended to supervise moving through rooms and reaching for objects.
Avoid fragile or sharp objects: use a clean plastic cup instead of glass, an empty clean egg carton instead of a real raw egg, and dull keys instead of sharp tools.
Keep small items out of reach of younger siblings who might place objects in their mouths.

problems.question: Which animal starts with the /m/ sound?
problems.rationale: Monkey begins with the /m/ sound made by the letter M. Snake begins with the /s/ sound, and tiger begins with the /t/ sound. Listening closely to the first sound helps identify words that start with M.
problems.teachingNote: Prompt students to press their lips together to feel the humming vibration when producing the /m/ sound in 'monkey'.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /m/ sound in a familiar spoken word
Distinguish the /m/ sound from other initial consonant sounds
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the /h/ sound?
problems.rationale: Hat begins with the /h/ sound made by the letter h. Pig starts with /p/ and nest starts with /n/. Practicing the breathy /h/ sound helps children connect initial sounds to familiar objects.
problems.teachingNote: Have students place their hand in front of their mouth when making the /h/ sound to feel the puff of warm air as they say 'hat'.
successCriteria: Identify words that begin with the /h/ sound
Distinguish the initial /h/ sound from other consonant sounds
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the /d/ sound?
problems.rationale: Dog begins with the /d/ sound made by the letter d. Sun begins with the /s/ sound, and cat begins with the /k/ sound. Saying the word slowly helps you hear the first sound at the very beginning.
problems.teachingNote: Have children place their hand lightly under their chin or touch their tongue to the roof of their mouth behind their teeth to feel how the /d/ sound is produced.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /d/ sound in a spoken word
Distinguish the /d/ sound from other initial consonant sounds
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word finishes this sentence: The playful ___ ran outside?
problems.rationale: Blending the sounds /d/, /o/, /g/ makes the word 'dog', which is an animal that can run outside. A hat or a pen cannot run on its own. This helps learners blend sounds together to make meaningful words.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to tap out each sound (/d/-/o/-/g/) on their fingers before blending. Remind them to think about which word makes sense in the spoken sentence.
successCriteria: Blend learned consonant and vowel sounds to read simple decodable words
Select the correct decodable word to complete a spoken sentence
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.statement: The letters 'c' and 'k' make the same primary beginning sound, like in cat and kite.
problems.rationale: Both the letter 'c' and the letter 'k' represent the hard /k/ sound at the beginning of words. Understanding that two different letters can share the same sound helps young readers decode new words more easily.
problems.teachingNote: Reinforce this concept by having students listen to the starting sounds of 'cat' and 'kitten' to hear that they match.
successCriteria: Recognize that 'c' and 'k' share the same primary sound
Identify the /k/ sound in common words
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: What word do the sounds /c/ /a/ /t/ make?
problems.rationale: When we slide the sounds /c/, /a/, and /t/ together smoothly, they form the word cat. A rat starts with the /r/ sound and a hen starts with the /h/ sound. Listening carefully to the starting sound /c/ helps us find the right match.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to tap each sound on their arm (shoulder, elbow, wrist) before sweeping their hand down to blend the whole word.
successCriteria: Blend individual phonemes /c/, /a/, and /t/ to identify a target CVC word.
